steps.content: Cold white light illuminates every tile of the floor evenly. The air is thick with the scent of formalin and disinfectant.
An autopsy table made of stainless steel stands at the center of the room, draped in a white shroud.
Forensica is already there, fully suited in protective gear, meticulously inspecting her autopsy tools.
The gleaming dissection instruments are laid out neatly on the surgical tray, cold and sharp.
Hope I'm not late.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: As the supervisor, I'd say... you barely made it on time.
Forensica looks far more composed and professional than yesterday. Her eyes are calm and focused.
You suit up in protective gear and a mask. The way you put on sterile gloves with practiced ease catches Forensica's attention.
I'm more than just a supervisor today. I'll also be your assistant.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Heh, to think I'll have the great MBCC Chief as my assistant. I bet most people would be trembling with excitement at such an honor.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: But you should know I'm not like most people. I'll call you out regardless if you mess up.
Forensica pulls away the shroud, revealing the body of a middle-aged man. You notice prominent wounds on his wrists.
She calmly proceeds with the autopsy, technical terminology coming out one after another from behind her mask.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: The deceased is a middle-aged male, approximately 175 centimeters in height, 70 kilograms in weight.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Horizontal wound observed on the wrist, approximately 1.2 centimeters in depth. Wound margins are clean, with minimal scabbing present.
Looks like suicide.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Congratulations on reaching the same conclusion as all those other idiots.
...I'm just stating what the evidence shows.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Yes, suicide. Simple and convenient. Who needs thorough investigations or questions when you can just chalk everything up to suicide, right?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Use your eyes. It's obviously not that.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Don't take it the wrong way. I'm not mocking you specifically. Most people are blind during an autopsy.
Forensica meticulously examines the wounds and skin, repeatedly verifying details as she voices her findings.
It's almost as if there's no need for any hypotheses when she's here—a single glance is all she needs to reach the most accurate conclusion.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Wound margins show slight retraction from post-mortem desiccation. There are no patterns typical of arterial spray or deep clotting from vascular rupture.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Meaning that the wrists were cut while the victim was dying or already dead. It's only staged to look like suicide.
Forensica lightly palpates the neck, finding exactly what she was looking for.
She raises her hand, gesturing for you to pick up the scalpel with forceps and place the handle in her palm.
Forensica makes an incision along the neck, her movements precise and efficient, just like a surgeon performing an operation.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Slight swelling above the thyroid cartilage. Petechial hemorrhaging visible beneath the skin.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Oral mucosa intact, though slight abrasions can be found in the posterior pharyngeal wall.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Facial cyanosis and ruptured capillaries in the nail beds. Consistent with asphyxiation.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Suicide after excessive drinking due to depression? Yeah right—

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: This is the Origami Killer's signature methodology. Using massive blood loss to mask the real cause of death—asphyxiation.
But if there's all this evidence available... why would they conclude that it's suicide and close the case just like that?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: What else? Career advancement, good optics, maintaining the illusion of peace and order...

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Serial killings cause public panic. Suicide, on the other hand, would never cause a ruckus, especially when the victim isn't anyone important. There's no need for them to dig any deeper than that.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: And the public only sees what those in power want them to see.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: As for the truth? It'll just be buried along with these bodies. No one cares anyway.
You open your mouth to say something, but ultimately decide against it.
Forensica isn't making baseless claims—what she describes happens all too often in reality. But your own experiences tell you that not everyone is like that.
You just hope she'll be able to believe in someone or something again, even if just a little.
According to the case files, the Origami Killer usually leaves origami flowers at the crime scene, but there doesn't seem to be any near this body.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: That's because they know I'm just a step away from finding them.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: I might not know who this bastard is right now, but one thing's for sure—I've been inching closer to the truth over the years.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: At first, the origami flowers were like a signature, a way for the killer to show off. They'd appear around the bodies.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: People knew the Origami Killer existed, but had no idea how they killed.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Suicide, homicide, accident, allergic reaction... When it comes to how the victims found near the origami flowers died, there were no patterns to speak of.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: But I knew better. I knew that it was all a cover-up and that they actually all died of asphyxiation.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: With enough samples, it was only a matter of time before I found the killer.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: And so, they stopped leaving behind origami flowers, hoping the bodies would blend in with routine deaths so that they could avoid getting exposed.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: But what hasn't changed is their method of killing. The killer is intelligent and cautious, but they're also arrogant and proud.
There are many ways to cause asphyxiation... And we can't eliminate the possibility of someone copying the method of killing either.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: ...You're quite interesting.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: I thought you'd be just another pretentious idiot, but it turns out you actually can get things done. You're quite sharp too.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: That wasn't a compliment. Smart people have it rough.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: The world's been taken over by idiots, and smart people are forced to play by their rules because of that.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: You've got a long way to go if you actually want to earn my recognition.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Well, you're already better than most people I've met though. Corpses included.
So, the key evidence is in the asphyxiation wounds?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: I extracted some fiber fragments from one of the victims' throats before.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: The killer would crumple a special type of paper into a ball before forcing it down the victim's throat, suffocating them.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: There's a significant amount of fibrin deposits around the hemorrhage sites, and the pattern matches the marks left by paper balls.
Forensica pulls a small glass vial from her pocket. Inside are dark brown scraps.
She holds the vial up to a shadowless lamp. Her pupils widen, eyes ablaze with fierce intensity.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: These are paper scraps I collected from one of the victims' throats.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: They were likely left behind when the killer removed the paper ball.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: After that, the killer grew more and more skilled, and left fewer and fewer traces behind.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: If I can extract fiber fragments of the same material from this corpse's throat, that would prove the Origami Killer's the one who did it.
You piece together the years-long battle between Forensica and this Origami Killer—two adversaries who have never met.
The Origami Killer would leave folded paper at each crime scene. It's a signature, a mark symbolizing another victory.
Forensica uncovered the victims' true cause of death, deciphered the killer's method, and recovered paper fragments as evidence.
The Origami Killer caught on. They grew more cautious, and more restrained. In subsequent cases, they stopped leaving origami flowers behind.
The killer might be extremely arrogant, but they're also intelligent and composed. They haven't lost control of themselves even once.
Without the origami flowers, no one but Forensica can trace the cases back to them.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: I swear I'll catch this bastard!
You seem particularly invested in this killer. Is there another reason why?
Forensica falls silent for a moment. She doesn't answer the question, and instead continues with the autopsy.
You assist by passing her tools and recording data. The two of you work together remarkably well, as if you've done this many times before.
Forensica extracts some more samples from several key areas and runs further tests.
She watches you record the data, and suddenly speaks.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Your hands are very steady. Nothing like those clumsy assistants I've had.
I've had some training before.
You flip through the recorded data. Just then, the edge of the paper cuts your finger.
The blood doesn't spread. You recall that when you were writing earlier, the paper seemed harder to write on than regular paper.
This paper is such a pain to use. Since we have to write without anything underneath it half the time, can't we use something easier to write on?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: What would you know? This paper is rigid enough and doesn't get stained by liquids easily. Not to mention, it's fire-resistant and easy to preserve.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: I've been using it ever since I was a student...
Forensica suddenly freezes in place. She seems to have realized something, her chest pounding.
She rushes to the lab bench and reaches for the glass vial containing the paper sample with trembling hands.
She then lifts the fiber sample from the vial using tweezers, and holds it over the flame of an alcohol lamp.
What are you doing? That's key evidence, isn't it?
Forensica stares at the fiber burning in the flame, eyes wide, breathing rapidly.
The fiber doesn't burn completely. Instead, a small fragment remains, even after being exposed to the fire.
Forensica's hand goes slack. The tweezers drop to the floor and clatter. She stumbles back, her face ghastly pale.
What did you find?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: How did I overlook something so simple...?
The shackles in your consciousness jolt suddenly. Forensica turns around and bolts to the door. She doesn't even remove her surgical gown or gloves, and simply rushes out of the morgue.
Her speed is staggering, and with her special power allowing for brief invisibility, she vanishes at the end of the corridor in an instant.
The next day, Chief's Office
Forensica vanished without a trace after yesterday. The burned sample sits on your desk.

She must have discovered something. That's why she reacted so strongly. You mobilized a search party overnight to track her down, but it wasn't until the following morning that you received news from Nightingale.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, the higher-ups have issued their report on Forensica's case and their ruling.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Forensica attempted to break into the DisCity University's School of Forensic Science last night. She was apprehended by security.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: She's currently being held on charges of disturbing the peace and unauthorized handling of potentially infectious remains.
At least we know where she is. Can you arrange for her to be transferred into our custody? Given her current state, she could easily lose control.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: I've already negotiated with them. They say she's emotionally stable at the moment, but she refuses to answer any questions. And since she escaped from MBCC custody, they're reluctant to send her back to us.
Nightingale shakes her head, then pulls out an evidence bag from her folder and hands it to you.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: However, I was able to secure a visit with her. She asked me to pass this along to you.
You take the evidence bag. Inside is a scrap of paper torn from a forensic record sheet. The words "School of Forensic Science" and a name are written on it.
Aster... Wynne?
Do you know anything about this person?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: I had someone look into her as soon as I received the note. According to our records, she's an outstanding graduate of the School of Forensic Science and happens to be Forensica's senior. She's a forensic pathologist with an eccentric personality, but her talent is undeniable.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: After graduation, she was expelled from both the School of Forensic Science and the Forensic Association for "misconduct."
Sounds awfully similar to Forensica.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Indeed. She appears to be another eccentric genius.
What was the reason for her expulsion?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: According to the Association's official statement, she "lacks reverence for life" and "places her own will above all else."
Those are pretty serious charges...

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: I interviewed several people connected to her, including former mentors and colleagues. They said she frequently altered autopsy procedures without authorization and even took tissue samples without permission to conduct experiments.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: She was also once authorized to conduct tests on critically ill or dying patients for data.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: But as her demands grew increasingly bizarre and cruel, she was ultimately expelled and blacklisted. The Association never disclosed the specifics of what she did either.
I take that back. Forensica is far better than her.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: After her expulsion, Aster vanished for a time before reappearing in the residential areas on the outskirts of Eastside.
Nightingale hands you another stack of documents and points to a particular section.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Shortly after that, the first Origami Killer case occurred.

The documents show that Aster, the expelled forensic pathologist, was once listed as a suspect in the Origami Killer cases. However, everyone who lived near her testified that she was just a shut-in who kept to herself, and they never noticed anything unusual about her.
As you flip through the pages, you notice that critical evidence, such as alibis and the like, is completely absent. She was cleared of suspicion based solely on a few flimsy testimonies.
You stare at the news article. If Forensica wanted to convey a message to you, it must be related to the culprit.
The burned paper fibers on the desk remind you of Forensica's words in the morgue.

Forensic recording paper is rigid and doesn't get easily stained by liquids. If someone crumples something like that into a ball and forces it down a person's throat, it'd make for the perfect murder weapon.
And if the killer is a forensic pathologist, she would know exactly how to forge wounds, conceal evidence... and choose her victims.
The case that led to Forensica's expulsion involved a victim named Eligy. The origami flower pattern at the scene matched those found in the Origami Killer cases.
Forensica discovered discrepancies and demanded further autopsy, but the victim's family suddenly withdrew their complaint and prepared for immediate burial.
In search for evidence, Forensica forcibly performed the autopsy, but was interrupted by the director and the victim's family. The incident was deemed a serious violation and led to her expulsion.
Even so, Forensica didn't give up. She set her sights on the Origami Killer and tried anything she could to uncover cases connected to the culprit.
Those stripped of their status become decadent, depraved, fading into obscurity.
It's something that has happened to Aster and Forensica alike, yet they walked completely different paths.
No one suspected that she would murder anyone, and no one noticed when she did either. Or perhaps... they did suspect something, but weren't allowed to voice it.
When power escapes the scrutiny of the public, those who hold it quickly become narrow-minded and arrogant.
Yet, such is life. It is a paradoxical thing that can bring hope and destruction all the same.
It's just like this forensic record sheet. It can be evidence that reveals the truth, or a weapon that enables murder.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, what do we do now?
Now that we know the truth, I intend to keep my promise. I will give Forensica the justice she seeks.
Both procedural and moral justice.
